Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Tim Seifert and Finn Allen walk in with their blades for New Zealand. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, New Zealand will be confident to chase down 92 runs and go 1-0 up in the series. Can they do it with ease or will the Pakistani bowlers show some fight and make it hard for them? We shall find out soon. Join us in a while for the second essay.

Kyle Jamieson is up for a chat. He revealed that he had discussed his bowling strategy with the skipper, opting to save an over for the back end due to the swing-friendly conditions here. He expressed relief at being back home and fit, following a tough year, and hoped his batting wouldn't be required.

New Zealand were brilliant with the ball. They utilized the conditions well and extracted good bounce and swing from the surface. Kyle Jamieson ripped through the top order and finished with an outstanding spell of 3/8 from his four overs. Jacob Duffy with four wickets also did a fine job while Ish Sodhi, and Zakary Foulkes also played their part nicely to dismiss Pakistan to an under-par score.

A sorry-looking scorecard for Pakistan who have been bundled out for just 91 and have failed to bat out their quota of overs. Having been sent into bat first, Pakistan were in all sorts of trouble early on and were reeling at 11/4 in the fifth over. Khushdil Shah and Salman Agha stuck a 46-run stand to provide some stability but both the batters were dismissed after getting to decent starts. Jahandad Khan stuck a few lusty blows down the order but the Men in Green failed to go past the 100-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities and all set for action to begin. Mohammad Haris and Hasan Nawaz stride out to open the innings for Pakistan. It will be Kyle Jamieson to start with the ball for New Zealand. Let's play...
The teams and match officials make their way to the ground for the National Anthems. We start with the anthem of Pakistan, followed by that of New Zealand. Live action is coming shortly.

Salman Agha, the skipper of Pakistan shares that it looks like a good wicket and they don’t feel it will change much. Adds that they are going with new combinations and he is excited for this young batch of players.

Michael Bracewell, the skipper of New Zealand has won the toss and opts to bowl. Says that it's a great wicket and adds that they will hope to utilise the bounce at the Hagley Oval. Shares that he is glad to get the captaincy armband in front of the home crowd and he is looking forward to it.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Haris(WK), Hasan Nawaz, Salman Agha(C), Irfan Khan, Shadab Khan, Abdul Samad, Khushdil Shah, Jahandad Khan, Shaheen Afridi, Mohammad Ali, Abrar Ahmed.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tim Seifert(WK), Finn Allen, Tim Robinson, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Hay, Michael Bracewell(C), Kyle Jamieson, Ish Sodhi, Jacob Duffy, Zakary Foulkes.
Toss Update - New Zealand have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

With a fresh squad and a point to prove, Pakistan will hope to start the series on a positive note. So, who do you think will take the early advantage? We'll find out soon. Stay tuned for the toss and team news!

On the other hand, Pakistan will be eager to bounce back after a disappointing exit in the Champions Trophy, where they were knocked out in the first round. The Men in Green have assembled a young squad, hoping to turn their fortunes around. Salman Ali Agha has been appointed captain, with Shadab Khan as his deputy. New faces like Abdul Samad, Irfan Khan, and Hassan Nawaz will bring added firepower, while Mohammad Haris, Sufiyan Muqeem, and Jahandad Khan add variety to the lineup. The pace attack will be spearheaded by Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, and Mohammad Ali, while Abrar Ahmed will look to carry his ODI form into the T20I series with his leg-spin.

New Zealand have been in solid form in the limited-overs format, but they will be missing a few key players for this series. The team will be led by Michael Bracewell and will rely on explosive batters like Finn Allen, Tim Seifert, and Mark Chapman. Daryl Mitchell and James Neesham provide all-round balance, while Will O’Rourke, Ben Sears, and Jacob Duffy will be pivotal with the ball, offering a strong challenge to Pakistan.

After finishing as runners-up in the recently concluded Champions Trophy, the Black Caps are set to host Pakistan for a limited-overs tour featuring five T20Is and three ODIs. A warm welcome to our coverage of the first T20I in the five-match series between New Zealand and Pakistan, from the Hagley Oval in Christchurch.
…MATCHDAY…

The 2025 cricketing calendar is packed with exciting fixtures and with the much-awaited return of the ICC Champions Trophy now out of the way, we are back to a bilateral series that is going to be played between Champions Trophy hosts Pakistan and Champions Trophy runners-up New Zealand. It will be Pakistan traveling to New Zealand for a couple of white-ball series' that include 5 T20Is and 3 ODIs and the tour will commence at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch with the 1st T20I. Both sides finished the Champions Trophy with a bit of disappointment as the Kiwis suffered another heartbreak in the finals, whereas Pakistan failed to reach the semifinals even after being the defending champions and playing at home and a lot has been made of that performance which has enforced a lot of personnel changes atleats for the T20I part of this series. New Zealand will also be without a lot of big names and will be led by Michael Bracewell who did have a good Champions Trophy and there are a few names retained from that squad with the likes of Will O'Rourke and Kyle Jamieson leading the bowling attack. A couple of seasoned campaigners return to the fore in the form of all-rounder James Neesham and leg spinner Ish Sodhi. The Kiwis do have a good mix of youth and experience, and with the focus now shifting to the T20 World Cup of 2026 to be played in India, a lot of players in this squad of just 13 will be looking to impress and try to get more of a starting role in the team. Pakistan, on the other hand, have a new-look team but they have also retained the likes of Haris Rauf and Shaheen Afridi from the Champions Trophy along with leg spinner Abrar Ahmed and it will be Salman Agha who will lead the T20I side. Shadab Khan, a former mainstay of the national side, also returns for the T20I series and he will play deputy to Salman Agha as they look to forego the blemishes of the Champions Trophy and usher in a new dawn. Hard-hitting top-order batter Mohammad Haris also returns and Usman Khan keeps his place but that batting lineup does feature a lot of inexperienced players and the likes of Hasan Nawaz and Abdul Samad might even make their debuts in this series. Right then, the Kiwis will have the home advantage and will be the more confident side but with so many changes in the Pakistan squad, they might not have the pressure of that Champions Trophy disappointment and in the end, it might turn out to be a fascinating contest. Who do you think will come out on top in the opening encounter?
